page: Amazon Web Services i8g.2xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by the AWS Graviton family using the Neoverse-V2 core microarchitecture at 2.8 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. It features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by 64.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware resource allocation combines 1875 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with a 5 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not feature dedicated graphics hardware or acceleration coprocessors. In benchmarking, the memory subsystem demonstrated standout throughput, recording a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3203.15 and large-block read-only memory bandwidth of 154.96 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression scored in the top 25 percent at 14.14 GB/sec, while general integer, compiling, and multi-core Geekbench tasks remained within median ranges.

Performance tradeoffs emerge in vector-heavy tasks, where the lack of AVX-512 and matrix hardware extensions impacts specific workloads. The PassMark encryption test showed lower throughput at 1507.35, placing in the lower quartile, and prompt processing for a 7B LLM model remained low at 15.47 tokens per second. However, the high memory density per core combined with high-speed local NVMe storage provides strong resource balance without relying on external network block storage.

Workload fit centers around I/O-heavy and data-intensive services, such as real-time NoSQL databases, transactional relational stores, search index nodes, caching clusters, and distributed logging pipelines that benefit from direct NVMe access and an 8-to-1 memory-to-vCPU ratio.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.2xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance built on the Nitro System using AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz. It delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory and 1875 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. The platform includes a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates exceptional memory throughput, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score and 154.96 GB/sec large-block read bandwidth. Compute performance across Geekbench and stress-ng tests sits solidly in median tiers, with strong single-threaded compression performance. While encryption and larger LLM inference workloads show architectural performance limits, the integration of direct NVMe storage and 8.0 GB of RAM per core makes this instance well matched for transactional databases, search engines, and real-time data processing nodes.
